description: Message body symbols (format specifier twice, data, EOS, ECC; 255 = garbled) -> parsed message fields, severity, ECC check and content id.

compare.method: Parse input.symbols; compare every key of `expected`. null means the field MUST be absent. Keys listed in a case's non_normative_fields are informative only.

All-ships call, SAFETY, with channel/frequency element.
Individual ROUTINE call carrying a position (55 prefix).
Individual call with RX and TX frequencies (6-digit form).
Individual call with an RX frequency only (TX = 126 no-info).

Individual call with different RX/TX HF/MF channels.
Distress alert: nature 107, position, event time, telecommand.
All-ships distress relay from a coast station (man overboard).
Damaged reception: garbled (255) symbols and wrong length.
Geographic area call.
area-call moved to the SW quadrant (quadrant digit 3): corner latitude and longitude negative.
Symbols decoded from the sample WAV recording (8414.5 kHz).
Format 114 (group with common interest) built from individual-safety.
Format 123 (individual, automatic service).
Individual call with category URGENCY (110).
Individual call with category ROUTINE (100).
TO is a group MMSI (one leading zero).
End of sequence ACK (122).
End of sequence 127.
First telecommand is 126 (no information) -> absent.
Distress alert with event time 88 88 (not provided).
Distress alert with position 99 99 99 99 99 (not provided).
Position in the SW quadrant (signed negative lat/lon).
VHF channel 16 (first symbol 90 -> channel form).
RX element 41 22 55 00 in the 7-digit form (HM 4): 12255.00 kHz (F-06). The TX element that follows, 92 25, has HM 9 with TM 2: kind unknown (F-15).
Two 7-digit elements (four symbols each): RX 12255.00 kHz, TX 12355.50 kHz (F-06).
VHF channel element 90 10 16: digit M = 1 (ship transmit frequency as simplex), channel 1016 (F-15).
Element 91 0 16: HM 9 with TM 1 is not defined: kind unknown (F-15).
Element 80 12 34: HM 8, ITU-R M.586 equipment: kind m586, no value (F-15).
Element 61 0 0: HM 6 is not defined (would be 6.1 MHz-class above 30 MHz): kind unknown, not a frequency (F-15).
All-ships distress acknowledgement (110) whose distress identity equals the sender: self-cancel (sec 8.6, Table A1-4.2).
allships-distress-relay with distress telecommand 110: an acknowledgement, not a relay (F-12).
Individual distress alert relay (112) from a man overboard device in closed loop: distress identity = sender = MOB identity 972123456. Not a self-cancel (sec 8.4, Table A1-4.3).
Distress alert with nature 112 (EPIRB emission, M.493-15 only): decoded as legacy (F-21).
Position request: first telecommand 121, message 2 = six 126 (Pos3), EOS 117 (Table A1-4.7).
Position acknowledgement: Pos4 (Pos1 + 126) and message 3 UTC 15:00, EOS 122 (F-13). Formerly decoded as 6228.00 kHz.
Position acknowledgement refusing the request: six 126, EOS 122 (M.493-16 Table A1-7).
Distress alert cut off before its EOS (the receiver gave up at its character limit): recorded, no EOS and no ECC, and no alert (F-27).
Distress alert with the second format specifier garbled: decoded, but format_unconfirmed, so no alert (sec 4.2, F-14).
All-ships call whose format copies disagree (116 vs 120): format_unconfirmed (sec 4.2, F-14).
Format specifier 103: call to ships in a VTS area (ITU-R M.825), with category URGENCY: never alerts (Table A1-3 note 3, F-16).
Category 103 (VTS, ITU-R M.825) (F-16).

ACS individual call (M.493-16 Table A1-4.9.2): category 106, second telecommand 122 = two ACS transmissions remaining. 122 is also an EOS value: the EOS is the one after the second telecommand (F-04, F-22).
Format 123 request with public network number 0012345 (105 00 01 23 45, sec 8.3.3) (F-17).
Format 123 request with public network number 00123456 (106 00 12 34 56, sec 8.3.3) (F-17).
Format 123 end-of-call acknowledgement (tc1 105, EOS 122): chargeable duration 00 06 50 = 6 min 50 s (ITU-R M.1082-1 sec 2.5.2 example), then the number.
End-of-call acknowledgement with six 126: duration not available.
Unsolicited end-of-call acknowledgement (EOS 127, Table A1-4.10.1 note 1): duration 01 02 03 = 3723 s.
End-of-call request (tc1 105, EOS 117): message 2 is a frequency, not a duration (VHF channel 16).
individual-position with latitude minutes 65: the position is absent (F-19).
distress-alert with an M.821 enhanced position resolution field 100 05 72 59 33 (M.821 sec 3.1 example digits): 62 deg 28.0572 min N, 006 deg 13.5933 min E (F-18).
expansion-position with the two 126 fillers of the first RX positions between the call and the expansion (M.821 sec 2.2.1).
position-ack followed by expan3 (Table A1-4.11: EOS 122) with enhanced position.

Expansion fields from the M.821 examples: 101 01 00 00 (differential GPS, HDOP not specified, WGS-84), 102 01 24 (12.4 kn), 103 02 98 (by the coding rule of sec 2.1.2.4: 29.8 deg; the example text says 298 deg, F-23).
Expansion field 104 26 19 13 15 29 41 03: station identification "PICES 3" (M.821 sec 3.4 example), and 106 00 12: 12 persons on board.
Expansion carrying data requests: 100 110 (position) and 104 110 (identification); 102 126 (speed: no data available).
expansion-position with the expansion's ECC changed: fields still decoded, expansion ECC fails, the call's ECC is unaffected.
Distress alert with time 25:61: the time is absent (F-19).
One garbled symbol inside FROM: FROM absent, ECC skips the garbled symbol.
First format specifier garbled; the second copy is used.
Format specifier copies disagree (120 vs 116); a known format is preferred.
Valid message with a wrong ECC symbol.
ECC symbol itself garbled: received/computed unavailable.
Unknown format specifier (100).
allships-safety with one content symbol changed and the original ECC kept; the tail EOS, ECC, EOS, EOS must not mask the error (F-04).
eos-repeated-bad-ecc with the ECC after the first EOS corrected.
No EOS symbol at all (reception cut short): EOS and ECC absent.
Category symbol garbled: category absent (not "unknown").
Empty symbol sequence.
A single symbol.
